content:
eli_support: FYI — customer E-376 (enterprise, EU dedicated) opened a high-priority ticket: sudden spike in latency and 5xxs since ~09:10 UTC. They say traffic is landing on hosted-us endpoints even though they have EU reserved capacity. ticket: https://support.redwood.com/t/E-376

anya_sre: @eli_support can you paste one request id / trace?

eli_support: trace: 9f7a2c4e-3d11-4b9c-b0f6-e3a11c2d1b2a. sample header from their repro: 
```
x-request-id: 9f7a2c4e
x-customer-id: E-376
x-region-preference: eu
x-route-decision: hosted-us-03
x-dedicated-pool: eu-ded-01 (expected)
```

devon_infra: thats bad. routing logs show a fallback to hosted-us when pool reported 'full' but capacity freed later. need to check TTLs on routing-affinity.

routing-bot: alert: route-fallback-rate > 0.5% for eu-dedicated pools between 09:07-09:20 UTC. sample keys: `affinity:E-376:node -> hosted-us-03`

anya_sre: hypothesis: affinity TTL refresh failed on the pool eviction path so requests kept getting sticky to hosted fallback even after eu-ded slot freed. could be race during eviction + async refill.

eli_support: customer provided repro steps. short loop they ran: 
```
# reproduce (customer):
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $E376_KEY" \
    -H "X-Region: eu" \
    -d '{"model":"gpt-eu-ded","prompt":"ping"}' | jq -r .route
  sleep 0.2
done
```
They see ~40% responses with route=hosted-us-03 and high token latency.

devon_infra: I pulled routing-store snapshot: when eu-ded pool reports 0 capacity we set fallback affinity -> hosted cluster with TTL 30m. On refill we attempt to delete affinity but if delete fails (transient redis error) the affinity stays. we rely on TTL to expire; but TTL refresh path was broken in 2.1.7 runtime.

anya_sre: runtime 2.1.7 had a fix for TTL refresh on canary but apparently it wasn't on prod cluster for EU. verify range: are we running 2.1.7 in eu?

devon_infra: eu-runtime-nodes: mix of 2.1.6 (60%) and 2.1.7 (40%). 2.1.6 had the bug where fallback affinity isn't garbage-collected promptly. that matches.

eli_support: immediate ask from customer: stop sending them to hosted-us and help with billing (they saw cost spike).

anya_sre: mitigation options (short):
- 1) override routing for E-376 to pin to eu-ded manually (routing-control) — immediate stop but risk overcommit if pool is actually full.
- 2) disable hosted fallback for E-376 — requests will return 429/503 if no capacity, but avoids cross-region latencies and billing surprises.
- 3) force push runtime 2.1.7 to all EU nodes (requires infra deploy, ~12min rolling).

devon_infra: I'll push 2.1.7 to eu canary now and follow with rapid roll. canary -> 3 nodes first. ETA 10m to canary, 25m full roll.

billing_ops: tagging in case credits needed. @billing_ops can you pre-approve emergency credit for E-376 for cross-region usage? they reported ~€1.2k increase in hosted consumption in the window.

billing_ops: acknowledged. can pre-authorize provisional credit up to €1500 pending postmortem. please add detailed usage logs.

anya_sre: short repro/debug steps for SRE:
1) query routing-store: `GET affinity:E-376` -> shows `hosted-us-03` + TTL 1794s
2) check pool health: `GET /_internal/pool/eu-ded-01` -> back to available capacity at 09:18 UTC
3) check runtime version: `kubectl -n eu get pods -o wide | grep runtime` -> 2.1.6/2.1.7 mix
4) look at logs for affinity deletion errors: `grep "affinity delete" /var/log/runtime/*.log | grep E-376` -> shows `ERR redis: connection reset` at 09:12

eli_support: customer-ops asked for a short-term route override until fix is in. prefer (2) to avoid silent overcommit.

devon_infra: done: routing-control override applied: `affinity:E-376 -> eu-ded-01, override=true, ttl=1h`, and hosted fallback disabled for E-376. responses now go to eu-ded (or return 503 when full).

routing-bot: action: routing override applied by devon_infra at 09:35 UTC.

eli_support: customer confirms route now eu-ded and latency normalized. they're happy with that for now.

anya_sre: plan: full rollout 2.1.7 to eu, then remove override and re-enable fallback with tested TTL refresh. postroll checks: affinity GC success rate, fallback rate < 0.1%.

devon_infra: starting roll now. will broadcast when complete and include metrics.

billing_ops: please gather the cross-region ingestion metrics for E-376 between 09:05-09:40 UTC and prepare a one-time credit. I'll include a note in ticket.

eli_support: thanks team. I'll update customer with temporary credit and expected timeline: 40min for full rollout. :thumbsup:

anya_sre: follow-ups: create a unit/regression test for affinity deletion on redis transient errors, and add an alert for stale affinities per-customer > 5m beyond pool-available time.

devon_infra: opened infra issue INF-5423. tagging for postmortem.

eli_support: closing loop — customer replied: "Thanks — routing fixed, latency back to normal, appreciated credit." closing ticket after billing reconciles.

customer-ops: noted for customer-facing postmortem.

routing-bot: summary metric: fallback-rate-eu-dedicated peaked 0.72% window 09:07-09:20. baseline prechange 0.03%.

anya_sre: marking as resolved after roll verification + billing credit. will file postmortem with timeline and root cause (runtime version skew + affinity TTL refresh regression).

eli_support: good work everyone.
